title: Iowa State Government Websites: ADA Title II PDF Accessibility | SignalFeed.dev
description: How Iowa state-government websites stand on PDF accessibility before the April 26, 2027 ADA Title II date: 24% of 439 sampled PDFs untagged, 6% scanned. Aggregate, automated signals.
h1: Iowa: Title II PDF backlog on state government websites
body:
We found 33 working state-government websites on .gov domains registered to Iowa in CISA's public .gov registry. State governments are Title II public entities, and all of them reach the ADA Title II web rule's compliance date on April 26, 2027 (28 CFR part 35, subpart H): web content, PDFs included, must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to the rule's exceptions.

Does ADA Title II apply to Iowa?

Yes. Title II is federal law and covers Iowa's state agencies and public universities, counties, cities, towns, school districts and special districts; the PDF guide covers the rule's exceptions. This is general information, not legal advice.

We measured the PDFs these sites link from their pages. This page summarizes Iowa's state-government sites as a whole. It does not name or rank individual agencies. Agencies on non-.gov addresses are not included. For cities and counties, see the city and county editions.

Iowa at a glance

  • 10 of 33 state-government sites measured with a usable sample (20 or more PDFs). Of the rest, 0 blocked our crawler and 23 could not be sampled: too few PDFs on the main site (some host documents on other systems) or a crawl that only partly finished. That is not a clean result.
  • 439 PDFs analyzed. 23.9% had no accessibility tags, lower than the national figure of 37.7%. 6.2% were scanned images with no usable text, 26.9% did not declare a document language, and 65% had no document title.
  • Spread: on 1 of the 10 measured sites more than half the sampled PDFs were untagged; on 2, fewer than 1 in 10 were. The most common main issue was no document title (6 of 10 sites).
  • 0 of 30 sampled PDFs passed the veraPDF PDF/UA-1 checks.
  • The median measured site has roughly 172 pages of PDFs failing at least one basic check; across the measured sites that is on the order of 28,000 pages.
  • 48% of the sampled PDFs were modified in 2024 or later. Recent documents are more likely to still be in active use, and documents used to apply for, access or participate in a service are not covered by the rule's exception for preexisting documents.

What this means for Iowa agencies

An untagged PDF gives a screen reader no headings, reading order or table structure, and a scanned one gives it nothing; both typically fail WCAG 2.1 AA and are common in reports, rules, forms and notices. Archived content and preexisting documents are exempt unless people use them to get a service, so the usual order is: fix export settings, remediate forms and service documents, then move true archives to a marked archive section.

For agendas, minutes and notices, our accessible meeting templates for small public bodies ($24, Word + PDF/UA) export tagged PDFs from Word, so new documents start out accessible.

What this is, and what it isn't

These are automated signals scaled from samples, not a conformance evaluation: a check can show a PDF fails, not that it conforms. Method: national Backlog Index page.

The Iowa workbook lists every state-government site we targeted in the state, with the registering organization, with PDFs found and estimated, untagged and scanned shares, recent-document share, estimated pages failing basic checks and days to the compliance date.
